This chicken biryani uses 1.1 pound (½ kg) skinless chicken pieces, 1½ cups (275 grams) aged basmati rice, and 6 cups water for boiling the rice. The marinade is ½ cup plain yogurt with lemon juice, ginger, garlic, spices and herbs.

First make the marinade: in a large bowl stir together the yogurt, lemon juice, ginger garlic, green chili, oil, salt, turmeric, Kashmiri red chili powder, biryani masala, coriander powder, cumin powder, mint and coriander leaves. Taste and adjust salt and heat. Make gashes over the chicken, add it to the marinade, and marinate at least 30 minutes at room temperature or overnight in the refrigerator.

Heat oil or ghee in a heavy bottom pan or Dutch oven on medium flame. Add sliced onions and sauté until golden to light brown, about 14 minutes. Remove them to a plate, keeping the excess ghee in the pan, and spread the onions out. Add the marinated chicken and sauté 4 to 5 minutes on medium heat, reserving 2 tablespoons of the brown onions for later and adding the rest.

Pour ¼ cup hot water over the chicken and cook covered on medium heat for 10 to 15 minutes, until the chicken is almost cooked through (about 95%) and the gravy is thick. Turn off the heat.

While the gravy cooks, rinse the rice well three times and soak it at least 15 minutes. In a large pot, pour the water and add the whole spices you have: cardamoms, cloves, bay leaf, cinnamon, star anise, shahi jeera and mace. Bring to a rolling boil, then add oil, salt and the drained rice.

Bring the water to a rolling boil again and cook on high heat for 5 minutes, until the rice is 90% cooked, then drain immediately into a colander. Meanwhile, soak the saffron strands in the hot milk plus hot water.

Once the chicken is cooked, layer 1 tablespoon of the brown onions over it, then spread all the rice over the chicken gravy. Sprinkle 1 to 2 pinches biryani masala, the mint and coriander leaves, ghee, the saffron milk water and the rest of the fried onions.

Cover and dum cook on medium heat for 5 to 6 minutes, then lower the heat to low and dum cook another 18 to 20 minutes. Turn off the heat and rest 10 minutes. If not using a Dutch oven, seal the pot with foil or a moist clean cloth so most of the steam is trapped.

Heat oil or ghee in a heavy bottom pan on medium flame, add the onions and sauté until golden to light brown, about 14 minutes. Pour ¼ cup hot water over the chicken and cook covered on medium heat for 10 to 15 minutes, until the chicken is almost cooked through (95%) and the gravy is thick. Turn off the heat. Meanwhile, rinse the rice well thrice and soak it at least 15 minutes.

In a large pot, add the whole spices to water and bring to a rolling boil. Add oil, salt and the drained rice, bring to a rolling boil again, and cook on high heat for 5 minutes until the rice is 90% cooked. Drain immediately into a colander. Also soak the saffron strands in hot milk plus hot water.

Once the chicken is cooked, layer 1 tablespoon brown onions over it, then spread the rice all over the chicken gravy. Sprinkle 1 to 2 pinches biryani masala, mint and coriander leaves, ghee, the saffron milk water, and the rest of the fried onions.

Cover and dum cook on medium heat for 5 to 6 minutes, then lower the heat to low and dum cook another 18 to 20 minutes. Turn off the heat and rest 10 minutes. If not using a Dutch oven, seal the pot with foil or a moist clean cloth so most steam is trapped.

Make gashes over the chicken, add it to the marinade and marinate at least 30 minutes at room temperature, or overnight in the refrigerator.

Cover and dum cook on medium heat 5 to 6 minutes, then on low heat another 18 to 20 minutes. Turn off and rest 10 minutes.
